legend: You have an intricate system of n%%ZSMJ0%% circular gears connected in a line, with their centers fixed in n%%ZSMJ1%% corresponding axles. The i%%ZSMJ2%%-th axle is fixed on the wall at coordinate xi%%ZSMJ3%% on the (imaginary) number line.

However, a massive earthquake just hit, and all gears have fallen to the ground, leaving the axles hanging on the wall. Given the radii of the n%%ZSMJ4%% gears ri%%ZSMJ5%% and the coordinates of the axles, you are asked to reinstall the system by putting the gears back onto their original places.
input: The first line of the input contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ6%% (1≤n≤500000%%ZSMJ7%%).
The second line of the input contains n%%ZSMJ8%% integers x1,x2,…,xn%%ZSMJ9%% (1≤xi≤1016%%ZSMJ10%%), the positions of the axles in increasing order.
The third line of the input contains n%%ZSMJ11%% integers r1,r2,…,rn%%ZSMJ12%% (1≤ri≤109%%ZSMJ13%%), the radii of the n%%ZSMJ14%% gears.
output: Output n%%ZSMJ15%% numbers s1,s2,…,sn%%ZSMJ16%% which indicate the correct placement of the gears on their axle. More specifically, si%%ZSMJ17%% should be the radius of the gear that will be placed on the i%%ZSMJ18%%-th axle from the left. For the placement to be valid, every two neighbouring gears must be touching, and s%%ZSMJ19%% should be a permutation of r%%ZSMJ20%%.
It is guaranteed that for all test cases, a solution exists. If multiple solutions exists, you may output any of them.
